findings: Production already exists and is called staging: straumvakt.org, api.straumvakt.org and ws.straumvakt.org all serve traffic and all three are bound to -staging Workers

S0 PROVEN: ws.straumvakt.org is served by straumvakt-ocpp-staging, demonstrated by tailing that Worker while requesting /health?probe= and watching the probe arrive. Same method proved api.straumvakt.org → hlada-api-staging

The dispatch's premise that top-level straumvakt-ocpp is the live charger gateway is WRONG — it returns 404/error-1042 on workers.dev and produced zero tail events in 25s while the staging gateway showed live traffic within seconds
There is no safe place to test: `wrangler deploy --env staging` on the gateway or API IS the production deploy

Two of the three production hostnames existed only in the Cloudflare dashboard and in no committed config — now declared, with workers_dev EXPLICIT because declaring routes without it infers false and would remove the workers.dev host with chargers behind it

The fleet may be split across two hostnames — both ws.straumvakt.org and the workers.dev host serve the live gateway, and ADR 0035 records chargers configured against the latter, so both must be preserved until device configs are audited

CORRECTION: the 'one-way door' claim carried since 2026-08-11 is wrong. `wrangler versions list` returns a full history and the live deployment has a prior version to roll back to. What is missing is runtime self-identification and a Sentry release id, not the ability to roll back

Option (c) rename is a trap and should be struck: changing `name` deploys a NEW Worker and leaves the old one running; secrets and Durable Object namespaces do not follow. Already why commit 4fe0a95 is on the RC exclusion list
A different Worker script means a different Durable Object namespace, so any cutover loses every charger's liveness, frame-cap and pending-command state

The dead-code comment in gateway/wrangler.jsonc was stale: the three UI-side OCPP paths are already deleted and OCPP_WEBHOOK_SECRET appears in no source file. Only the secret survives, on the unreachable top-level hlada
My own golden-file tests carried a latent cross-platform defect (A's CR-1) that passed here for exactly the reason it would fail on any fresh Windows clone
Straumvakt-core-security holds no unique work: 0 dirty, 0 commits ahead, 0 unmerged
blockers: Q1 — does anything outside engineering inspect infrastructure resource names? It is the only condition that flips the recommendation from option (a) to (b)
Q2 — can a Worker bind to a Durable Object namespace declared by a different script via script_name? Decides whether any future rename costs one reconnect or every charger's durable state
Q3 — does the gateway still authenticate chargers with CHARGER_BASIC_AUTH? Only blocks options (b)/(c), where dropping it would stop all 21 chargers reconnecting
Release-checklist item 4 remains undone: the invoice validator has still not run against a GENERATED invoice, because A's branch carries none
Neon point-in-time-restore window is unknown — it is what makes A's 0002 rollback window real

Audit the 21 chargers' device configs to learn which hostname each uses
Write down the three current version ids — sixty seconds, and the rollback capability already exists

All three public hostnames serve traffic from -staging Workers, and S0 — ws.straumvakt.org → straumvakt-ocpp-staging — is now PROVEN by tail-and-probe rather than inferred, refuting the dispatch's premise that top-level is the live gateway.
